title: Shared identifiers in entity resolution
summary: Which identifiers raise a suggestion when you resolve entities, what each one does and does not show, and what is skipped.

paragraphs: Besides email addresses, the index reads three California-relevant identifiers. A suggestion can say two names share one. A shared identifier is a reason to look, not proof that two names are one party, and nothing is merged for you.

sections.heading: What is read
items: EIN: ten characters in the form NN-NNNNNNN with an assigned IRS prefix, standing alone. A bare nine-digit number is never read as an EIN. The format is all that is checked; no checksum exists.
Contractor license: six to eight digits directly after a label such as CSLB or Contractor License, or after Lic. No. when the word contractor is on the same line. Format only.
Parcel number (APN): NNN-NNN-NN or NNN-NNN-NN-NN directly after APN or Assessor's Parcel. Format only.
Values that the app's privacy masking would remove are not indexed.

sections.heading: What each one can link
items: An EIN can link organizations, never people.
A contractor license can link people or organizations.
A parcel number identifies a property. It never links people or organizations: two parties named near one parcel are neighbours of that parcel, not each other.

Both names must appear within a short stretch of text (about 200 characters) of an EIN or license number, in at least two documents each. Only the first mention of each name in a passage is measured, so a closer later mention can be missed.

sections.heading: What is skipped
paragraphs: An identifier tied to more than the allowed number of names (8 for an EIN or license, 12 for an email address) is skipped as a template value or shared mailbox. The Resolve entities panel shows how many were skipped.
Documents indexed before this feature need to be re-indexed before these identifiers appear. The app does that automatically the first time it opens an older index.
